<reason>This was a genuinely close, high-quality debate. B built the more memorable frame — marginal returns, the willingness gap, and above all the unaware, unwitnessed, non-MAT decedent ("he doesn't know he is a drug user") — and used it to expose PRO's weakest answer, forcing A onto supervised consumption sites that barely exist in the U.S. and test strips the boy would never buy. That was the single most damaging blow of the debate. But B's affirmative route required interdiction/penalties to actually change supply composition favorably, and A kept that burden alive and unmet. When A's Pressure Q1 demanded a single era where supply disruption bent national mortality, B's cleanest answer was Australia's heroin drought — and A's closing dismantled it in one stroke by noting heroin has a harvest to fail while fentanyl regenerates in a lab. B's fallback (regional timing of the current decline) went unanswered but is a weak causal link to any enforcement lever, since B itself attributes it to a maturing supply's own composition shift rather than to policy. A also answered the "you conceded composition decides mortality" trap coherently (accept premise, reject direction: enforcement's record is heroin→fentanyl→nitazenes), and A's attack on trafficking penalties sweeping up replaceable low-level couriers — half of the motion B had to defend — was never rebutted at all. A's effect-size grounding (MAT roughly halves mortality, naloxone acts at the point of death) is more ordinary and secure than B's plausible-but-untested precursor/pill-press chokepoint mechanism. B also incurred a small execution cost with a clipped over-length opening. Net: B landed the sharper single hit; A's structural route to victory survived the exchange more intact.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's closing distinction on B's Australia heroin-drought example — a crop-based supply that could collapse versus a synthetic that regenerates in a lab — neutralized B's only clean natural experiment and restored A's central "no interdiction era ever bent the mortality curve" burden. B's counterpunch, exposing that A's answer to the unwitnessed overdose rests on two legally besieged consumption sites, was the closest rival.</best_rebuttal>
